name: Pseudo Linear Multistep Sampling
definition: A sampling method for diffusion models that uses a linear multistep predictor (Adams-Bashforth) to estimate the noise residual at the next timestep, allowing for fewer function evaluations per step compared to standard Euler or Heun methods, while maintaining stability similar to DDIM.
summary: Pseudo Linear Multistep Sampling accelerates diffusion model inference by estimating noise residuals using a linear multistep predictor, reducing function evaluations while maintaining stability.
